questions.text: The primary purpose of a business, as defined in the course glossary, is to:
opts: Provide goods and services to customers to achieve profit
Eliminate all competition in the market
Employ as many people as possible
questions.explanation: Business provides goods and services to customers with a profit objective.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: Which business form is generally owned and managed by one person?
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship is owned by one person.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: A major disadvantage of a sole proprietorship is:
opts: Lack of direct control by the owner
questions.explanation: The owner can be personally responsible for business debts.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: A partnership agreement primarily helps partners to:
opts: Remove the need for business decisions
Define the terms of their business relationship
questions.explanation: The agreement records the partners’ arrangements.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: A corporation is distinguished by:
opts: Being owned by only one person in every case
A separate legal identity from its owners
Having unlimited liability for every shareholder
questions.explanation: A corporation has a legal identity separate from its owners.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: A rise in interest rates is primarily an example of a change in the:
questions.explanation: Interest rates are an economic factor.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: Which is part of a business’s specific environment?
opts: The general level of technological development worldwide
questions.explanation: Customers and suppliers are specific stakeholders.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: Government regulation can help protect consumers by:
opts: Preventing every business from making profit
Removing the need for product standards
Setting and enforcing relevant safety standards
questions.explanation: Regulation can establish and enforce safety requirements.

questions.text: An entrepreneur’s central role is to:
opts: Identify opportunities and assume the risk of starting a venture
Purchase products only for personal use
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs identify opportunities and take risks.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: Which of the following is a manifestation of organisational culture?
questions.explanation: The course lists five manifestations of culture: corporate values, organisational climate, management style, organisational behaviour and structure. Exchange rates and inflation are macroeconomic conditions, not culture.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which factor represents the beliefs and values of an organisation's founders?
questions.explanation: Founders' philosophy is the first listed influence on culture: the beliefs, values and leadership approach of the founders establish the organisation's original culture, which later practices build on.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which of these is an effect of organisational culture?
questions.explanation: Culture shapes employee attitudes and behaviour, and the course lists motivation, labour turnover, productivity and efficiency as its effects. Ocean currents, rainfall and latitude are physical-geography distractors.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What is the first step in the cultural transformation approach described in the Miva case study?
questions.explanation: Step 1 of the case-study model is a cultural assessment: examine existing norms and practices to identify what needs to change BEFORE redefining values or launching programmes.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Who is expected to help redefine Miva Company's values?
questions.explanation: The case study specifies a cross-functional team - people from different parts of the business collaborating - so new values reflect the whole organisation rather than one group's view.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which activity helps build the capabilities needed for cultural change?
questions.explanation: Training programmes (step 3): they develop the skills and behaviours employees need to actually live the desired culture; ignoring performance or stopping training undermines change.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which factor can influence organisational culture through past practices and traditions?
questions.explanation: Organisational history: accumulated experiences, traditions and past decisions shape current attitudes and 'how things are done here'.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Why should an organisation continuously evaluate cultural change?
opts: To monitor progress and make adjustments
questions.explanation: Step 5 of the model: continuous evaluation monitors progress and allows adjustments - without it, the organisation cannot tell whether the change is taking hold or drifting from its goals.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is NOT listed in the course summary as a manifestation of culture?
questions.explanation: The summary lists management style, organisational structure and organisational climate (among others). Exchange-rate policy is a government macroeconomic instrument, not a cultural manifestation.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: A positive organisational culture can contribute to which outcome?
opts: The end of all organisational change
questions.explanation: The course links positive culture to improved collaboration, engagement and performance. It does not guarantee profits, eliminate competition, or end change - those options overstate the effect.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_week12_quiz (key authored from course content)

questions.text: A measure used to track progress towards a business target is called a:
questions.explanation: A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is a measurable value that tracks progress toward a specific target. A CSF identifies the critical AREAS that must go right; it is not itself a measure.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which of the following is a financial KPI?
questions.explanation: Revenue growth is measured directly in money terms. Employee morale, waste reduction and customer loyalty matter, but they are non-financial (operational/qualitative) indicators.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: A critical success factor identifies:
opts: The essential areas for achieving organisational goals
questions.explanation: CSFs are the essential areas where things must go RIGHT for the organisation to achieve its goals - e.g. quality or customer service - not routine activities or expenses.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is an example of an intrinsic reward?
questions.explanation: Intrinsic rewards arise from the personal satisfaction of the work itself: achievement, autonomy, growth, purpose. Commission, salary and allowances are financial (extrinsic) rewards.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is a non-monetary reward?
questions.explanation: Professional development (training, growth opportunities) rewards without direct payment. Profit sharing, salary and commission are all financial payments.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: The main purpose of total reward is to:
questions.explanation: Total reward COMBINES financial elements (pay, bonuses, benefits) with non-financial ones (recognition, development, work-life balance) to motivate employees as a whole, rather than relying on pay alone.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which of these is an external driver of organisational change?
questions.explanation: New government regulations originate OUTSIDE the organisation and force adaptation. Leadership succession, low morale and internal restructuring are internal drivers.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which principle helps reduce resistance to change?
questions.explanation: Employee engagement: involving people in the change builds understanding and ownership. Withholding information fuels rumour and fear, which increase resistance.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Improving an existing production workflow is an example of:
questions.explanation: Process innovation: finding better ways of doing existing work. It contrasts with product innovation (new goods/services) and is not a reward or a KPI.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: A business reviews performance data and corrects problems. This illustrates:
questions.explanation: Continuous performance improvement: systematically reviewing results and fixing problems in an ongoing cycle - the opposite of resistance to change, and unrelated to segmentation or intrinsic motivation.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_additional_10 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which form of business is generally owned by one individual?
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship: one person owns, usually manages, receives the profit and personally bears the risks and liabilities (course model answer). Partnerships involve two or more owners.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is an example of an economic factor affecting a business?
questions.explanation: Inflation is an economy-wide condition in the business environment (it raises input and borrowing costs). A logo, a job title or office seating are internal business decisions.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Who primarily identifies business opportunities and assumes entrepreneurial risk?
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur: the course's answer guide distinguishes the entrepreneur - who spots opportunities and bears risk - from the manager, who coordinates resources and runs operations.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What is the main purpose of most business activities?
opts: To satisfy needs and wants, usually for profit
To employ every member of society
questions.explanation: The course defines business as the production or provision of goods and services to satisfy needs and wants, usually for profit - satisfying customers IS the route to profit, not an alternative to it.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Who starts a business and takes the risk of running it?
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur starts the venture and carries its risk; consumers buy, workers provide labour, auditors only check records.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: A business owned by one person is called a:
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship - the simplest ownership form: one owner who typically manages the business, keeps the profit and bears unlimited liability.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What is one main advantage of a partnership?
opts: Partners can combine skills and capital
questions.explanation: Partners pool capital, combine complementary skills and knowledge, and share responsibilities - the course's three listed advantages. Disagreements are a known risk, not an advantage.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is an example of an external business factor?
questions.explanation: Government policy comes from outside the firm and shapes what it may do (taxes, regulation). Staff morale, management style and internal procedures all originate within the business.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which of the following is part of the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: Promotion - one of the four Ps (product, price, place, promotion). Recruitment is HR, auditing is accounting; warehousing is logistics, not one of the four Ps.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What is market segmentation?
opts: Dividing a market into customer groups
questions.explanation: Dividing a heterogeneous market into distinct customer groups (by need, income, location or behaviour) so each group can be served and targeted more effectively.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which statement best describes accounting?
opts: Recording, analysing and reporting financial transactions
questions.explanation: Accounting is the process of recording, analysing and REPORTING financial transactions so stakeholders can make informed decisions - far broader than any single activity like selling or paying salaries.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What does a balance sheet show?
opts: Assets, liabilities and equity at a given date
questions.explanation: The statement of financial position shows assets, liabilities and equity AT A GIVEN DATE, expressing the accounting equation: assets = liabilities + equity.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is a fixed cost within a relevant activity range?
questions.explanation: Rent stays the same regardless of output within a relevant range. Raw materials, per-unit commissions and packaging all vary directly with the level of activity, making them variable costs.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which inventory consists of products still being manufactured?
questions.explanation: Work in progress: partly completed goods still on the production line. Finished goods are complete; office equipment is a fixed asset; accounts receivable is money owed.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What is the main purpose of stock control?
questions.explanation: To maintain suitable inventory levels: enough stock to meet demand without tying up capital in excess inventory or suffering stockouts and lost sales.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which HR function involves finding suitable applicants for a vacancy?
questions.explanation: Recruitment: attracting and identifying suitable candidates for a vacancy. Selection (choosing among them), training and appraisal come later in the HR cycle.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is a monetary reward?
questions.explanation: A salary is a direct financial payment. Personal pride, praise and sense of achievement are intrinsic (non-financial) rewards - they satisfy psychological needs, not financial ones.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What does a KPI measure?
opts: Performance against an objective or target
questions.explanation: A KPI measures performance against a specific objective or target (e.g. monthly sales growth). It is a forward-looking management tool, not a record of history or personality.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What does a CSF identify?
opts: A company's daily cash balance only
A factor critical to organisational success
questions.explanation: A CSF identifies a factor CRITICAL to organisational success - the limited set of areas where things must go right, such as product quality or customer trust.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which can influence organisational culture?
questions.explanation: Founders' philosophy is the course's first-listed influence on culture. The building's colour, computer count or bank balance are not among the four influences (founders, history, socio-cultural factors, competitors).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What is change management?
opts: Managing movement towards a desired future state
questions.explanation: Change management is the structured process of moving an organisation from its current state to a desired future state - guiding people, processes and culture through the transition.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is a likely reason employees resist change?
questions.explanation: Fear and uncertainty: people resist when they cannot predict how change will affect their jobs, status or routines - which is why communication and training reduce resistance.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which action can help an organisation encourage innovation?
questions.explanation: Encouraging useful ideas and improvement: welcoming suggestions and rewarding experimentation fosters innovation. Punishing ideas, silencing staff or ignoring customers suppresses it.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA_practice_test_1 (key authored from course content)

questions.text: According to the course's Section B model answer, business is defined as an activity involving:
opts: Production or provision of goods and services to satisfy needs and wants, usually for profit
questions.explanation: The model answer defines business as production/provision of goods and services to satisfy needs and wants, usually for profit.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA 101 short-answer Q1

questions.text: Which is a characteristic of a sole proprietorship per the course?
opts: Owned by two or more people
The owner bears the business risks and liabilities
questions.explanation: The model answer: one owner, usually self-managed, receives profit, and bears risks and liabilities.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA 101 short-answer Q3

questions.text: Which is an advantage of a partnership listed in the course?
opts: Partners combine capital, skills and shared responsibilities
questions.explanation: The model answer lists combining capital, combining skills and knowledge, and sharing responsibilities as partnership advantages.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA 101 short-answer Q5

questions.text: In the course's comparison, the PRIMARY distinction between an entrepreneur and a manager is that the entrepreneur:
opts: Identifies opportunities and assumes business risk
questions.explanation: The answer guide: the entrepreneur identifies opportunities and assumes risk; the manager coordinates resources and makes operational decisions.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA 101 Question 3

questions.text: Which set of business-environment factors does the Nigerian business terrain reading identify?
opts: Political, economic, social, technological, ecological and legal
questions.explanation: The guide lists political, economic, social, technological, ecological and legal factors affecting Nigerian businesses.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA 101 Question 2

questions.text: The marketing mix component among the following is:
questions.explanation: Promotion is one of the marketing mix elements; the others listed are business functions outside the mix.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA 101 Practice Test 1 Q6

questions.text: A balance sheet (statement of financial position) shows:
opts: Assets, liabilities and equity at a given date
questions.explanation: The course describes the balance sheet as showing assets, liabilities and equity at a given date.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA 101 Practice Test 1 Q9

questions.text: Government intervention in business is justified in the course by all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The answer guide lists regulation, consumer protection, fair competition, public welfare and compliance - not eliminating private enterprise.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - BUA 101 Question 4

questions.text: Theory Y (McGregor) assumes that people inherently:
opts: Avoid responsibility and need close control
Want to work and can exercise self-direction
Work only to satisfy hygiene factors
questions.explanation: Theory Y holds that work is natural and employees can exercise self-direction and self-control.

source.label: Introduction To Business MCQs and Answers (mcqss.com) - key authored from standard management theory

questions.text: The process of grouping jobs into logical units within an organisation is known as:
questions.explanation: Departmentalisation is the grouping of jobs into logical units such as departments or divisions.

source.label: Introduction To Business MCQs and Answers (mcqss.com) - key authored from standard management theory

questions.text: Which personnel are directly responsible for achieving organisational goals?
questions.explanation: Line personnel hold authority in the direct chain of command and directly accomplish the organisation's goals.

source.label: Introduction To Business MCQs and Answers (mcqss.com) - key authored from standard management theory

questions.text: Entrepreneurs tend to be:
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurial traits commonly cited include optimism and a willingness to accept calculated risk.

source.label: Introduction To Business MCQs and Answers (mcqss.com) - key authored from standard management theory

questions.text: For an entrepreneur, a business plan serves as:
opts: Only a document for bank loans
A realistic evaluation of the venture's chances, its risks, and a game plan for managing the business
questions.explanation: A business plan evaluates the venture's prospects, identifies key risks and acts as the management game plan.

source.label: Introduction To Business MCQs and Answers (mcqss.com) - key authored from standard management theory

questions.text: Goods can be divided into:
questions.explanation: Consumer goods are commonly classified as durable or nondurable.

source.label: Introduction To Business MCQs and Answers (mcqss.com) - key authored from standard management theory

questions.text: Franchising involves a ________ vertical marketing system.
questions.explanation: Franchise systems are a form of contractual vertical marketing system linking franchisor and franchisee.

source.label: Introduction To Business MCQs and Answers (mcqss.com) - key authored from standard management theory
